It was one of those deep, writhing stretches, the kind where you can feel every muscle in your body pull tight and release and it is the best way to start a day. My mouth tasted like shit, a product of too much beer and terrible food the night before, but I wanted coffee first and I could brush my teeth while I checked my news feed. Shuffling down the hallway, I enjoyed the peaceful saturday morning. No traffic, no neighbors screaming, no police sirens, it was rather nice. I knew it wouldn't last long, even on the outskirts of Houston, so I basked in the silence while it could hold out. I entered my kitchen and stumbled over something lying in the floor - my dog, Zuke, had somehow wriggled out of his collar again, and left it lying in the middle of the floor. I sighed and grinned as I picked it up, and called for Zuke. Of course there was no answer, he always hid after shedding his collar, it was one of his favorite games and as stupid as he was he never hid in the same place twice in a row. I called again, listening for the telltale movement or thump of his tail as he eagerly awaited discovery. He was extra silent this morning. I decided to start the coffee brewing before I started the search for Zuke. I laid Zukes collar on the counter and reached for the coffee pot, filling it with water. I noticed the coffee pot wasn't on, so I reached for the plug but it was plugged in. I unplugged and plugged it in several times to no avail. Fuck it I thought, and moved to the cabinet to get an instant coffee bag. I retrieved a bag and turned to the microwave, and noticed that the microwave was also off. Slightly irritated now, I reached for the stove to see if it would come on, and it didn't. Knowing the power was out, I still headed for the living room to see if the TV would come on - it didn't, but I now noticed the left side of the french door was cracked. I slid back the curtain over the right side and nearly expelled the contents of my stomach.

The right side of the French door was mostly shattered, with pieces laying all over the balcony, my lawn chair, and Zukes partially mutilated body. It looked like Zuke had just...dove through the door. This sweet dog, who had never harmed a thing, never barked unless someone excited him, who always patiently and quietly waited for me to feed him or let him out, now lya at my feet brutally sluaghtered. I choked back my tears and closed the curtain back, not wanting to disturb the scene. I quickly went back to my bedroom and grabbed my cellphone. Dead. I had forgotten to plug it in before I crashed last night, fuck. I plugged it in now, but I knew before I did that there was no power. I quickly got dressed, so I could borrow a neighbors phone. I was hoping there would be CCTV footage of the heartless fuck who broke into my house and killed my dog. I grabbed my car keys and locked the door behind me, hoping the cops would be quick. The hallway was dark, very dark. Apparently power was out in the whole unit. My apartment was at the end of the hallway, so there was one apartment across from mine, and the rest were down the hall. A woman in her mid forties named Svetlana lived across from me, she also had a dog that she loved dearly, I'm sure she would would let me borrow her phone. I knocked on her door and waited.

After a moment with no answer, I knocked again, louder. Still no answer, so I went to the next apartment down the hall, the one next to mine. No answer there either. I decided to skip the rest and go straight to hte office on the ground floor, I knew they would take care of it, especially with property damage involved. I slowly bagan to notice, on my way down the nearly pitch black stair well, that everything was still silent - deathly so. Far more silence than I had ever heard. I exited the stairwell and was nearly blinded by the morning sun, streaming in through the plate glass lobby foyer. I went to the receptionists desk, which had been abandoned. I now began wondering if something was going on, maybe the building had been evacuated, or there was a holiday that I was unaware of. At this point I decided to simply go to the police station myself, it was less than a mile away afterall. I turned to walk outside, and froze at the front door. What I saw out in the street is still chilling, just recalling the still vivid memory.

Cars were everywhere, some overturned, many on fire, still others had crashed into eachother or into buildings. A news chopper had fell from the sky and slammed into the foyer of the complex across the street, igniting the entire first floor it seemed but had already burned out. A fire truck was parked long ways across the street, hoses ran out and everything, but just as abandoned as everything else. Huge smoke clouds reached towards the sky everywhere, unanswered and uncontrolled. Somehow, it seemed, I had slept through some kind of horrid disaster without so much as a toss or turn. I cautiously opened the door, and shakily stepped outside, expecting an explosion or collapse of some sort. Just as I felt as though maybe everything had reached a point of calm, an explosion rocked the area. I still don't know exactly where it came from, possibly several blocks away, behind my apartment complex. I finally pulled myself to my feet, and made my way down the street. The destruction I saw looked like a war zone. In the miles I walked that day, toward Houston proper, I might have seen 100 cars that were not wrecked or on fire There were military vehicles all over the place, many abandoned, and many destroyed - humvees, armored vehicels, a few tanks, all abandoned or burning - or burned out.

There were also there occasional downed plane, some were smaller single seat craft, but I saw at least two commercial airliners, one embedded in the side of a building that had collapsed somewhere along the 15th floor and fell over into another building. Traffic lights and other electrical signs were all out, and many store fronts had been smashed out, likely due to looting. I also noted that most apartment buildings had almost no glass left intact - even penthouse suites had been smashed, which I found odd even though I was in utter shock at what I was seeing everywhere. Other than the odd explosion and the ever present sound of a fire of some sort crackling, there was pure silence. No sirens, no voices, no animals, nothing at all. It was deeply unsettling to say the least. I rounded a corner, and found yet another sight that managed to astonish - and bewilder. A naval aircraft carrier lay in the street, or rather, lay wedged in the street. The buidings to either side were too close to accomadate such a vessel, so the keel had slammed against on building as the deck dipped low to the other side, buried into the buildings on the other side. Another oddity than my brain chose to notice at this moment, was a distince lack of bodies - living or otherwise. Besides myself, my murdered dog was the only remnant of a beating heart that I had seen in miles. It was all so surreal, and I was so lost in thought, that I nearly died of a heart attack when something slammed into the pavement right in front of a shop no more than 100 yards away. I screamed out loud, and dove behind a wrecked car. Bits of dirt and "asphault gravel" rained everywhere for a few moments. I stayed behind the car for a few more minutes before summoning the courage to stand up and take a look. There was a massive crater in the street now, but all seemed calm beyond that. I slowly approached the crater and peered inside. It appeared to be the reamins of some kind of satellite, and though burned up pretty badly, I could still make out the NASA logo on one of the panels.

What the fuck was going on, I wondered. It was getting dark, and I was too far from home to make it back with no light at all. I found a hardware store a couple of blocks away, and managed to scrape together a small bag of battereis and flashlights, enough to get me to some food - if there was any. There was a grocery store not far away so I made my way towards it. Many of the fires that had been so common during the day had burned out, leaving the night in it's natural form - blackness, at the mercy of nature and the moonlight. The grocery store had surely been looted, I assumed, but this one seemed mostly intact. I used a flashlight to smash out a window and then I waited and listened, hearing only the smae eerie silence that had so filled the past day. I went inside, and gathered some food. The store had a small camping section so I also grabbed a tent and sleeping bag. I decided to stay indoors for the night, since I didn't know what was going on outside. Entering that rear of the store, I stopped to blockade the "Employees Only" door, and laid out my stolen sleeping bag. I didn't know what was going on, or if there was anybody else in the city, but I was tired and mentally strained. I would further explore and try to find some people the next day. I fell into an uneasy sleep, filled with the wildest machinations of my stressed mind.

pt 2:

I awoke in a sleeping bag, and the scenes of destruction came rushing back to me. I had been wrapped in a cocoon of nightmares and horrid dreams, wishing, hoping the whole time to awake in my bed. I wanted so badly to wake up in my bed, to the shrill sound of my alarm clock, to the sound of Zukes tal thwapping aginst a cabinet door or his wet nose nudging my hand to let me know his belly was calling for food. Instead I was awoken to the sound of a deep, unnerving klaxxon, a sound I didn't hear as much as I felt in my bones. It started off loud and deep, ending in an impossibly deep, warbling grumble that I think fell below the threshold of human auditory capabilities, because I could feel it long after the sound ceased. It stopped as suddenly as it had started, but that did nothing to ease my nerves. I quietly rolled the sleeping bag up, and with the tent and bag I eased my way to the blockaded door and peered through the small window. There was nothing new, nothing out of place, so I unstacked my blockade and opened the door.

I made my way through the store, down an aisle toward one of those island coolers. Just as I reached the cooler, I heard the same deep, growling sound again. It permeated the very ground, emmanating from everywhere it seemed. I grabbed the island for stability, as everything shook. The sound stopped once again, still rippling though my body and the building for a few moments longer, just like before, then stopping. Just as I took a step, I heard a noise outside the store. It was like some kind of wild animal call, echoing off the city environment, bouncing back and forth several times. For whatever reason, I didn't feel like going out the front door at that moment. In fact, I felt a little scared of what could be out there, I don't know why. I quickly made my way back to the rear of the store, thinking to head to the dock area that most grocery stores had. I reached the loading dock, finding that one of the bay doors was open about 2 feet or so, with a hand cart rammed under it. I crept closer, and knelt down to look under. Just as I got a look outside, I heard the animal screech again. This time from inside the store.

I scrambled under the bay door, shoving my bag and tent before me, and lept to my feet. The dock was the type that dipped into the ground, and the entire alley was taken up by it, ending at the street some 200 or so feet away. There was a single dumpster off to one side, and that was it. I could hear something crashing around inside the store, making a hell of a racket, and I could tell it was getting closer to the back of the store. I did the only thing I could - I ran toward the dumpster. I tried not to make too much noise as I lifted the lid and nearly vomited. The dumpster was filled with all the rotten refuse from the store, as well as christ knows what that random bums and passers by had thrown in it. THe smell was overpowering, but I crawled in anyway, gently lowering the lid back down. It seemed to take forever but whatver was in the store finally reached the bay door. What sounded like metal on metal, as well as it screeching, then it sounded as if the bay door had been thrown all the way to the ceiling. After the deafening echo ceased, there was a click-clack sound, and the occasional guttural grunt. I dared not peek, and my curiosity was well over powered by fear. This went on for several minutes, the sounds drawing closer then further from the dumpster. Then the creature let out another screech, this one far louder and longer. All I could hear after that was something flapping, getting more and more quiet.

I don't know how long I sat in that fucking dumpster like a terrified fool. It must have been hours, because by the time I finally found the courage to take a peek, the sun was high in the sky and the heat within the container was nearly unbearable - as well as the stench of curdled milk and rotten meats. I didn't see the creature anywhere, so I tumbled out of the dumpster, taking great gasps of the fresh, cool air. As I lay on my back on the concrete ramp, I rolled my head toward the bay door, and saw that it had been torn completely free of the railing meant to hold it in place. The door itself was laying against an inner wall, some 50 feet inside the building. I didn't think much of it, and sat up. I decided to go back to the hardware store and find a bag, come back here and get some more food, and then head out. I had family in Dallas, maybe I could find them and figure out what in the hell had happened. After getting the food, I headed for 45 North, several miles away. Maybe I would find a truck or motorcycle that hadn't been completely wreck or locked. Maybe.
